chunks: And who is more unjust than he who invents a lie about Allah or says, 'Revelation has been sent down to me,' when no revelation was sent down to him; or he who says, 'I will reveal the like of what Allah revealed?' If you could see when the wrongdoers are in the agonies of death and the angels are extending their hands (saying), 'Give up your souls!' Today you will be recompensed with the punishment of humiliation for what you used to say about Allah other than the truth and that you were arrogant toward His signs.
ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for those who falsely claim revelation or speak about God without truth?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the concept of *al-Adil* (the just) and the specific arrogance of those who fabricate divine speech, such as the *Mubtala'ah* (those who claim to receive revelation). The 'humiliating punishment' (*'adhab al-haw*) is interpreted not merely as physical pain but as the spiritual degradation of having their truthfulness stripped away before the angels. This connects to the broader Shia emphasis on the authenticity of the Prophet's message against false claimants like Musaylimah or later Gnostic sects.
